title: Java Checked Exceptions and Annotations
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of java checked exceptions and annotations using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Java Checked Exceptions and Annotations** as part of **Kotlin and Java Interoperability**. Catch or represent expected failures at a boundary where the program can respond usefully; do not silently swallow errors or expose secrets in messages. Use the subtopics—Exception Handling Across Languages, @Throws, Nullability and Other Java Annotations—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

items.title: Nullability and Other Java Annotations
items.text: Nullability and Other Java Annotations is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.

fun parseCount(text: String): Int? = text.toIntOrNull()

fun main() = println(parseCount("not-a-number") ?: "Invalid count")

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Catching every exception and ignoring it is a safe recovery strategy.
